Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a retrial next year, a judge has said, after a jury deadlocked last time in a case that gripped the nation. The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face. Prosecutors said they wanted a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy, 36, would again face first-degree murder charges. Five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan were strangled at the family home on 24 January 2023. The defence argues she had severe postpartum psychosis. "I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA [district attorney] that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments, so we will pick a trial date," defence lawyer Kevin Reddington said at Monday's hearing. Petruska Abstract Linear motion components are widely used in antenna metrology positioning systems, but long motion ranges can reduce positioning accuracy due to the difficulty of eliminating rail component non-linearity. Further, offset device-under-test (DUT) mounting can magnify rotation errors arising from slight variations of rail parallelism not captured by a strictly linear motion model. We present methods to reduce position and rotation inaccuracy through kinematic calibration using a Legendre polynomial model. pages.text: Lionesses in Nations League draw: England draw France and Portugal - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Image caption, All the Uefa Nations League ties will be played over two legs By Sally Freedman BBC Sport senior journalist Published 3 November 2026 England have been drawn to face France, Austria and Portugal in next year's Women's Nations League. In Nyon, Switzerland, Sarina Wiegman's side were drawn alongside familiar opponents, having faced Portugal in the previous Nations League campaign, while France and Austria have both been recent rivals in major tournament qualifying campaigns. The Lionesses will begin their campaign in Group A2 across three international windows in February-March, April and June 2027, with each team playing home and away fixtures. "[France are] a world-class team," said Wiegman. "They have so much quality, they have power, they have technique and they have some players, of course, also playing in the WSL [Women's Super League] and at other top clubs. "So it's exciting to play them because you will be challenged in the highest possible way and that's what makes us better. "We played Portugal before the last Euros, when we tied with them away and at home we beat them. "They're a team who can change their style from playing a possession game to being a little more direct, and they have some players that bring lots of quality on the pitch, but are also powerful in duels." Lisa Daley Mangi Lisa Daley Mangi Lisa Daley Mangi is the General Counsel for the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). As the chief legal officer for the NNSA, Ms. Mangi advises the Administrator and senior NNSA leadership on all legal matters. She also oversees and provides strategic guidance to the 32 attorneys and professional staff who represent the agency in administrative litigation and provides counsel to NNSA programs on procurement, intellectual property, national security, environmental and other legal matters. Ms. Mangi served as the NNSA Deputy Counsel for Procurement, Intellectual Property, and Technology Transfer for NNSA from 2021 to 2025. Before she joined the Department of Energy, she was a trial attorney for the National Labor Relations Board. Ms. Mangi is a graduate of the University of Wisconsin and the University of Maryland School of Law. Articles by Lisa Daley Mangi

pages.title: List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor The Bureau of International Labor Affairs (ILAB) maintains a list of goods and their source countries which it has reason to believe are produced by child labor or forced labor in violation of international standards, as required under the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act (TVPRA) of 2005 and subsequent reauthorizations. The List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor comprises 204 goods from 82 countries and areas, as of September 5, 2024. The Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act of 2018 directs that the List include, "to the extent practicable, goods that are produced with inputs that are produced with forced labor or child labor." ILAB maintains the List primarily to raise public awareness about forced labor and child labor around the world and to promote efforts to combat them; it is not intended to be punitive, but rather to serve as a catalyst for more strategic and focused coordination and collaboration among those working to address these problems. pages.title: List of Products Produced by Forced or Indentured Child Labor | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: List of Products Produced by Forced or Indentured Child Labor | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content List of Products Produced by Forced or Indentured Child Labor ILAB maintains a list of products (also known as List of Products Requiring Contractor Certification as to Forced or Indentured Child Labor ) and their source countries which it has a reasonable basis to believe are produced by forced or indentured child labor, pursuant to Executive Order 13126 . This List is intended to ensure that U.S. federal agencies do not procure goods made by forced or indentured child labor. Under procurement regulations, federal contractors who supply products on the List must certify that they have made a good faith effort to determine whether forced or indentured child labor was used to produce the items supplied. If you need 508-compliant versions of these files, please contact GlobalKids@dol.gov . Read More ›› Excel Format Bibliography The Department of Labor, in consultation with the Departments of State and Homeland Security, publishes and maintains the List. ILAB released its initial List in 2001, and has revised it several times since then. As of October 3, 2016, the EO List comprises 35 products from 26 countries. Legal Authorities The List is required by Executive Order 13126 , "Prohibition of Acquisition of Products Produced by Forced or Indentured Child Labor." The procurement requirements related to products on the List are set out in a 2001 Federal Acquisition Regulation Final Rule .https://www.dol.gov/admin/appearance Procedural Guidelines ILAB develops the List us

Introduction Lithium batteries are vital components in many everyday consumer products, such as cell phones and backup power storage units. They play a crucial role in the rapidly growing U.S. markets for vehicle manufacturing, energy storage, medical services, and agricultural technology. These batteries also may contain important minerals and materials, including lithium (Li), cobalt (Co), and nickel (Ni), which are essential for many technologies driving U.S. commerce. Credit: Megan King/NIST Four years ago, NIST researcher Cyrus Daugherty developed an algorithm to virtually unroll the tightly wrapped layers of a cylindrical lithium-ion battery. Daugherty’s software transformed X-ray images of the battery, taken at different angles, into a CT scan. The scan, a 3D portrait of the battery’s interior, pinpointed hard-to-spot defects and highlighted wear and tear on its electrodes. This study aims to extend the life of lithium-ion batteries , which power everything from laptops and cellphones to e-bikes and electric cars. Lithium A relatively rare element, lithium is a soft, light metal , found in rocks and subsurface fluids called brines. It is the major ingredient in the rechargeable batteries found in electronics such as your phone, hybrid cars, electric bikes, digital cameras, laptops, and even large, grid-scale storage batteries. As a “critical mineral” necessary for rechargeable electric batteries, lithium has been identified as a material essential to the economic or national security of the United States. Researchers have been exploring how geothermal brines brought up to the Earth’s surface as part of geothermal power production may also be a critical resource for future lithium supply. pages.text: Living with dementia in southern Africa is a heartbreaking challenge | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE Living with dementia in southern Africa is a heartbreaking challenge In a region where family members have historically served as caretakers for older relatives, proper care for an aging population has become more difficult. Titus Ihemba, who lives in a care facility, is attended to by his daughter on a rare visit to his village in Rundu in northern Namibia. Care for older people in Africa usually falls to families, with informal kinship networks serving as one of the primary ways to look after the aging population. Photographs by Lee-Ann Olwage Text by Leonie Joubert Published June 22, 2022 Namibia, Africa — Relatives of Ndikuhoole Johanna Nakamhela began noticing the changes eight years ago when she struggled to recall significant moments in her life. She also seemed anxious when mingling with members of her church, something she’d done easily in her decades as a minister’s wife. These changes weren’t typical of the normal aging process, her doctor said, and a brain scan confirmed as much. Now, when the 77-year-old Nakamhela potters in her kitchen at home in Kalkfeld, a small town just north of the Namibian capital, a caregiver hovers nearby to ensure that she doesn’t leave a pot unattended on the stove or get into trouble with an open gas flame. Her changing brain state often seems to trap her in a private inner world. But other times, her body language indicates she’s content, even when words fail her. LM Information Technology Specialist Kyle Brown accepted the award on LM’s behalf. The EPEAT award recognizes organizations for excellence in sustainable procurement of electronic equipment. pages.text: Lobito Corridor: Can Trump-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo and Angola? Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo? 3 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Akisa Wandera BBC Africa, Lobito AFP via Getty Images The Lobito Corridor links DR Congo's mineral-rich south to Angola's Atlantic coast through the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito As trains carrying thousands of tonnes of copper from the Democratic Republic of Congo roar through her community, 20-year-old Manuela Julia is not thinking about critical minerals or billion-dollar investments. She is thinking about getting around more easily. The railway runs through Catumbela, near the Angolan city of Lobito, on the Atlantic coast. For Julia, it has made travelling cheaper and more convenient. "Before, I had to use a taxi, which is much more expensive. Now it is cheaper and easier to travel," she says. But the railway has ambitions far bigger than improving local transport. It is part of the Lobito Corridor, a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals and promote regional economic cooperation, which Washington hopes will help bring peace to conflict-torn eastern DR Congo. Under agreements brokered by US President Donald Trump, DR Congo and neighbouring Rwanda have committed to greater economic cooperation, including more transparent mineral supply chains and regional infrastructure development. pages.text: London City forward Izzy Goodwin receives first England call-up - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Izzy Goodwin has scored three goals in five WSL appearances for London City By Emma Sanders BBC Sport women’s football news reporter Published 17 November 2026 London City Lionesses forward Izzy Goodwin has been named in the England squad for the first time for the World Cup qualifying play-off against Ukraine. The 23-year-old has been in great form this month and scored in front of England manager Sarina Wiegman at Emirates Stadium on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Arsenal. "We have always seen her as a huge talent with potential," Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live. "I think London City are developing really well in the games they have showed. She is tall and can head a ball attacking-wise, but also defending. "She is really quick with her feet and can score goals. Long COVID Basics For Everyone May 6, 2026 Español Key points Long COVID is a serious illness that can result in chronic conditions, require comprehensive care, and can sometimes cause disability. Long COVID can include a wide range of ongoing symptoms and conditions that can last months to years after COVID-19 illness. Anyone who had a SARS-CoV-2 infection, the virus that causes COVID-19, can experience Long COVID, including children. Following core strategies to lower your risk of severe COVID-19 illness is the best way to prevent Long COVID. Living with Long COVID can be difficult and isolating, especially when there are no approved tests that can determine if your symptoms or conditions are due to Long COVID and there are no approved treatments. About Long COVID Long COVID is defined as a chronic condition that occurs after SARS-CoV-2 infection and is present for at least 3 months. Long COVID includes a wide range of symptoms or conditions that may improve, worsen, or be ongoing. Talk to your healthcare provider if you have symptoms that last for months after an infection. Long-Duration Energy Storage Background From providing critical backup power during natural disasters to supporting more renewable energy coming online, energy storage technologies make the grid more flexible and resilient. Today’s energy storage technologies are not sufficiently scaled or affordable enough to meet energy demand that fluctuates throughout the day and night. Long-duration energy storage (LDES) is a cost-effective option to increase grid reliability and resilience so that reliable, affordable electricity is available whenever and wherever to everyone. DOE defines LDES as storage systems capable of delivering electricity for 10 or more hours in duration. BABAK TAFRESHI, National Geographic Image Collection By Stefanie Waldek Published August 20, 2026 Stargazing can feel overwhelming when you don’t know where to begin. But in August, three exceptionally bright stars offer an easy starting point. Vega, Deneb, and Altair form the Summer Triangle, an enormous star pattern that rises high in the evening sky across much of the Northern Hemisphere. Once you find it, the triangle can serve as a guide to nearby constellations, deep-sky objects, and the Milky Way. It is also one of the most photogenic regions of the summer sky in August. Here’s how to find the Summer Triangle—and photograph what surrounds it. How to Find the Summer Triangle The Summer Triangle is not a constellation, but an asterism, or a recognizable pattern of stars. Begin with Vega, one of the brightest stars visible from Earth. In mid-August, observers in the Northern Hemisphere can generally find it high overhead. Deneb appears to one side of Vega, while Altair lies farther away, creating a large, elongated triangle. Here's why it happens and where to look. Venus, the Pleiades star cluster, and the bright star Capella rise in the dawn sky above a tufa formation in California’s Mono Lake. BABAK TAFRESHI, National Geographic Image Collection By Stefanie Waldek Published November 12, 2026 Look low in the northeastern sky on an autumn evening, and you might spot something unusual: a bright star flashing red, green, and blue. That’s Capella, one of the brightest stars in the night sky. But despite appearances, the star isn’t actually changing colors. The dazzling display is an optical effect caused by starlight passing through Earth’s atmosphere. And Capella isn’t the only star that puts on this kind of show. “Stars appear to twinkle or shimmer in the night sky, but this is not an inherent trait of stars,” says Emily Watson, astrophysicist and planetarium supervisor at the U.S. Space & Rocket Center. “As the light from a star passes through different densities and temperatures within our atmosphere, the light bends in a process called refraction.” The color flashes happen because Earth’s atmosphere bends different wavelengths of light by different degrees. pages.text: Looking for whales—and awe—in Baja California | National Geographic TRAVEL Looking for whales—and awe—in Baja California The Gulf of California was once known as “the aquarium of the world.” But on a recent whale watching trip—and in an era where climate change is making its mark—our writer wonders if it still delivers. The Sea of Cortez is famous for its marine mammals, including fin, minke, humpback whales, seals, and sea lions, as well as common and bottlenose dolphins. Story and video by Kinsey Gidick Published May 15, 2026 When considering a trip to Baja, it’s nearly impossible to dodge the words of two famous men: Jacques Cousteau and John Steinbeck. The pioneering French oceanographer famously called the Gulf of California “the aquarium of the world.” Not surprisingly, that line shows up everywhere—typed into brochures and slipped into itineraries, hovering like a promise. Meanwhile, Steinbeck’s The Log from the Sea of Cortez , the Pulitzer winner’s account of his 1940 six-week, 4,000-mile expedition examining tide pools and collecting specimens along the narrow sea is practically required reading. To be fair, the acclaim is well earned. Steinbeck’s account reads like a dispatch from another, more poetic, planet. But these touchstones sketched a vision of abundance so vivid, especially in a climate-anxious age, that they almost felt like fables: beautiful, sure, yet just distant enough to raise my eyebrow. Los Mirlos: Tiny Desk Concert September 17, 2026 10:00 AM ET Felix Contreras Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castillo/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Originally born from Afro-Colombian communities, cumbia spread across the Spanish-speaking world , acquiring distinct musical accents along the way. In Peru, cumbia became particularly popular among oil workers deep in the Amazon. And when Jorge Rodriguez Grández started Los Mirlos in his small hometown of Moyobamba, his band played a regional style called cumbia amazónica, easily identifiable by its electric, reverb-heavy, surf-rock guitar. Sponsor Message Alt.Latino Cumbia: The Musical Backbone Of Latin America Los Mirlos' time behind the Desk is not only a joyful celebration of this music but also a trail of small towns and cities throughout the Amazon jungle. Throughout their performance, these cultural ambassadors share stories and declare their love for cumbia and their tropical homeland. We are so fortunate to host and share with you a group of true pioneers and innovators who, over 50 years later, still effortlessly pump out cumbia grooves. Los Texmaniacs ' music is a living history lesson. The conjunto sound is driven by the button accordion, a mid-19th century instrument that made its way to the U.S.-Mexico border by way of German, Czech and Polish immigrants. But this music is also just perfect for twirling on the dance floor to songs about true love, heartbreak, folk heroes and reflections on life. Sponsor Message Alt.Latino Los Texmaniacs keep tradition alive Tiny Desk Flaco Jimenez: Tiny Desk Concert In this band, everything goes back to Flaco Jimenez , the late Tex-Mex accordion master whose rootsy sound came to define conjunto . Los Texmaniacs band leader and bajo sexto player Max Baca had a long-standing musical partnership with Jimenez — they played the Tiny Desk together in 2012 . And accordionist Josh Baca, Max's nephew, studied at the feet of Jimenez.
